newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says Bangui truce extended for a month.
newsitem.headline: France says Bangui truce extended for a month.

text.p: France, which helped negotiate a ceasefire between army mutineers and loyalist soldiers in the Central African Republic capital Bangui, said on Monday the truce had been extended for a month.
The extension of the two-week truce was announced at the weekend in Bangui, just before it was due to expire. But the duration remained unclear.
"We are pleased to note that a fresh one-month truce was agreed," the French Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
It said the two sides would use the truce to work on lasting solutions to ensure national reconciliation.
The agreement followed more than a week of difficult talks chaired by former Malian military ruler General Amadou Toumani Toure, who had been joined later by the French ambassador.
Thousands of Bangui residents have fled to the countryside fearing a resumption of the fighting. The mutiny erupted over pay grievances on November 16 and degenerated into tribal bloodletting.

French troops based in the former colony under bilateral accords helped keep President Ange-Felix Patasse in power during a violent mutiny last May and have been backing loyalist forces in the latest revolt.
